improvement_detail: every magma generator fails at least two tests that PCG64 passes; the longest periods available to order-2 recurrences (n^2 symbols) are far too short for practical use, and affine generators inherit the known low-bit weaknesses of lagged Fibonacci/multiple recursive generators
limitations: A sanity battery, not TestU01 or PractRand.
novelty_basis: Low-bit periodicity of additive generators modulo 2^w and the non-uniformity of Fibonacci numbers modulo 2^k are classical (Knuth, TAOCP vol. 2, 3.2.2; H. Niederreiter, Fibonacci Quart. 10 (1972) - uniform distribution only modulo powers of 5).
statement: On a simple battery (byte chi-square, serial pairs, lowest-bit period, lag-1 correlation; 2^20 outputs) the anchored Fibonacci and affine magma generators on Z/2^32 fail low-byte uniformity and have lowest-bit period 3, and the de Bruijn byte magma (maximal possible period 65536) is too regular; PCG64 passes every test.
title: Magma Fibonacci generators are not competitive pseudo-random generators
